newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock fund inflows slow this week - survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock fund inflows slow this week - survey.

text.p: About $3.47 billion in cash flowed into U.S. stock funds during the week ended Sept 26 versus $5.8 billion last week, according to a survey by Trim Tabs Financial Services.

"It's basically because money into aggressive growth funds declined," said Charles Biderman, Trim Tabs president. "Growth and income funds remained the same." He also cited a somewhat choppy U.S. stock market for some of the decline.

Biderman estimated about $730 million flowed into international stock funds, compared with $200 million last week. Bond funds had inflows of $1.5 billion versus outflows of $280 million last week. Muncipal funds had inflows of about $850 million versus outflows last week of $700 million.
Biderman said on Thursday he expected inflows for the full month to total about $24 billion, with about $20 billion into U.S. stock funds.
The Investment Company Institute said Thursday that $17.93 billion flowed in U.S. stock funds in August.
